name: Varun Beverages Ltd
about: Varun Beverages Ltd has been associated with PepsiCo since the 1990s and is a key player in beverage industry and one of the largest franchisee of PepsiCo in the world. The company produces and distributes a wide range of carbonated soft drinks, non-carbonated drinks and packaged water sold under trademarks owned by PepsiCo. PepsiCo brands produced and sold by the company include Pepsi, Seven-up, Mirinda Orange, Mountain Dew, Tropicana Juices and many more. [1]

sections.one_liner: PepsiCo's largest non-US bottler. Revenue growth is back at 33%, but EBITDA margin fell 141bps and PAT grew only 13.5%.
business: Largest PepsiCo franchisee outside the USA. Makes and distributes PepsiCo brands in 10 franchise and 4 distribution territories from 50 plants. [AR CY25]
India is 67% of revenue with 38 plants. International is 33% with 12 plants, mainly Africa plus South Asia. [AR CY25]
By volume: carbonated drinks 73.9%, packaged water 20.2%, non-carbonated 5.9%. Low/no-sugar rose from 59% (CY25) to 73% (H1 CY26). [AR CY25][Q2CY26 call]
PepsiCo supplies brands and concentrate. VBL funds capex and distribution. The agreement now runs to April 2049 and SPV restrictions were removed. [AR CY25][Q2CY26 call]
financial_snapshot: Q3 CY26: revenue Rs6,608cr (+33.2% YoY), EBITDA Rs1,424cr (+25.0%), PAT Rs831cr (+13.5%). EBITDA margin 21.5% vs 23.0% a year ago. [Numbers]
TTM: revenue Rs25,931cr, EBITDA Rs5,914cr (22.8% margin), PAT Rs3,480cr. The June quarter alone made 43% of TTM PAT. [Numbers]
ROCE 19.7% and ROE 16.2%, down from 29% ROCE in CY23. Book value Rs57.9 means 6.8x price-to-book. [Numbers]
Market cap Rs1,32,425cr at 39.1x P/E. Price Rs392 is 3% above the 52-week low and 30% below the Rs556 high. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR is 18.1% over 3 years and 27.4% over 5. Growth slowed to 8.4% in CY25 (weather) and recovered to +23.8% for 9M CY26. [Numbers][Q4CY25 call]
Over 3 years PAT grew 25.5% a year, faster than revenue, as OPM rose from 19% to 24% (CY20–24). OPM has now flattened at 23%. [Numbers]
9M CY26: EBITDA +19.9% and PAT +15.5% vs revenue +23.8%. Earnings now grow slower than sales, reversing the earlier margin gains. [Numbers]
ROCE peaked at 29% in CY23 and fell to 20% in CY25. Net worth nearly tripled (Rs6,937cr to Rs19,578cr), far faster than earnings. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings fell from Rs5,431cr (CY23) to Rs2,508cr (CY25). Debt/equity went from 0.78 to 0.13, and consolidated net debt is only Rs25.6cr. [Numbers][Q4CY25 call]
Net worth rose Rs9,673cr in CY24 against PAT of Rs2,634cr. About Rs7,000cr came from outside earnings; the source is not disclosed. [Numbers]
Working capital days moved from -47 (CY20) to +31 (CY25) and debtor days from 8 to 21. Working capital now uses cash instead of funding the business. [Numbers]
cash_quality: Cash from operations was 1.19x PAT over 3 years. In CY25 it was Rs3,509cr vs PAT Rs3,062cr, so profits do turn into cash. [Numbers]
Implied capex was about Rs11,400cr over CY22–25 and total FCF was -Rs325cr. Operating cash went into capex; the debt paydown was funded outside operating cash. [Numbers]
CY25 FCF of Rs797cr was the first clearly positive year. India capex guided at Rs500–600cr should lift CY26 FCF; Twizza cash outflow not disclosed. [Numbers][Q1CY26 call]
narrative_vs_numbers: Volume story holds: 20%+ growth guided after June, and Q3 revenue rose 33.2% YoY. How much came from the Twizza acquisition is not disclosed. [Q2CY26 call][Numbers]
Margins don't match: management said it would 'comfortably maintain' them, but EBITDA margin fell 123bps YoY in Q2 and 141bps in Q3. [Q2CY26 call][Numbers]
Management cites 30% ROCE on new plants, but group ROCE fell from 29% to 20%. Room for 50% more volume means much capacity sits idle. [Q1CY26 call][Numbers]
Q3 PAT rose 13.5% vs EBITDA +25%, so costs below EBITDA are rising. Depreciation rose 28.4% in CY25; Q3 breakdown not disclosed. [Q4CY25 call][Numbers]
guidance: Volume: at least 20% growth after June. India double digits over the medium term, and double digits for 5–10 years overall. [Q2CY26 call][Q1CY26 call]
Margins: consolidated EBITDA at 21% or above on a sustained basis. India at 22–23%, below the current 26% peak. [Q4CY25 call]
Capex: India Rs500–600cr in CY26. Existing capacity can handle 50% volume growth without new plants. [Q1CY26 call]
Distribution: add about 500,000 outlets on a 4m base in CY26, i.e. +12.5%. [Q1CY26 call]
Portfolio: South Africa growth of 80%+ in CY26. Rs10 packs capped at 5–7% of portfolio. Snacks to about $100m in 2–3 years. [Q4CY25 call]

ledger.promised: India volume back to double digits once weather improves. [Q3CY25 call]
ledger.delivered: India volume +10.5%. Revenue Rs4,204cr, +14.0% YoY. [Numbers][Q4CY25 call]

ledger.promised: International growth back to early-to-mid teens from next quarter. [Q3CY25 call]
ledger.delivered: International volume +10%, below the 13–15% target. Segment revenue not disclosed. [Q4CY25 call]

ledger.promised: Double-digit India volume growth in CY26, if weather is normal. [Q4CY25 call]
Consolidated EBITDA margin at 21% or above, sustained. [Q4CY25 call]
Raw materials fully covered for Q2, so margins should be protected. [Q1CY26 call]
ledger.delivered: EBITDA margin 27.2% vs 28.5% a year ago. EBITDA +16.5% vs revenue +21.8%. [Numbers]

ledger.promised: At least 20% volume growth continues after June. [Q2CY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Revenue +33.2% YoY to Rs6,608cr. Volume and Twizza share not disclosed. [Numbers]

ledger.promised: Can comfortably hold margins despite geopolitics and cost inflation. [Q2CY26 call]
ledger.delivered: EBITDA margin 21.5% vs 23.0%. PAT +13.5% vs revenue +33.2%. [Numbers]

ledger.promised: India capex Rs500–600cr. No major capex this year. [Q1CY26 call]
ledger.delivered: CY26 cash flow not reported yet. CY25 implied capex was about Rs2,712cr. [Numbers]

bull: 9M CY26 revenue up 23.8% with capacity for 50% more volume. Extra sales need little capex, which should lift ROCE and FCF. [Numbers][Q1CY26 call]
Debt/equity 0.13, cash from operations 1.19x PAT, AAA rating. CY26 India capex of Rs500–600cr is below CY25 FCF of Rs797cr. [Numbers][Q4CY25 call][Q1CY26 call]
PepsiCo deal extended to 2049, removing the AR's top risk. Low/no-sugar at 73% of volume reduces exposure to health regulation. [Q2CY26 call][AR CY25]
bear: EBITDA margin fell 123bps YoY in Q2 and 141bps in Q3. Q3 PAT +13.5% against revenue +33.2% means profits lag sales. [Numbers]
About Rs11,400cr capex over CY22–25 produced -Rs325cr total FCF. ROCE fell from 29% to 20%, well below the 30% plant target. [Numbers][Q1CY26 call]
Analyst said Campa is growing 50% at Rs10; VBL caps Rs10 packs at 5–7%. Debtor days up from 8 to 21 hint at more trade credit. [Q2CY26 call][Q4CY25 call][Numbers]
questions: Of Q3's 33% revenue growth, how much was Twizza versus organic?
Why did Q3 PAT grow only 13.5% when EBITDA grew 25%?
Debtor days went from 8 to 21. Is trade credit being used against Campa?
With room for 50% more volume, when does ROCE get from 20% back to 30%?

annual_report.business: VBL is the world's largest PepsiCo franchisee (outside USA) manufacturing and distributing carbonated soft drinks, juices, sports drinks, and packaged water across 10 franchise and 4 distribution territories. India represents 67% of revenues. PepsiCo provides brands/concentrates; VBL handles manufacturing, distribution, and capital allocation.

segments.name: International
segments.comment: Africa, South Asia, others; 12 facilities; growing

segments.name: Carbonated soft drinks
segments.comment: 73.9% of sales volumes (Pepsi, Mountain Dew, etc.)

segments.name: Water & juices
segments.comment: Packaged water 20.2%, NCB 5.9% of sales volumes

annual_report.revenue_mix: India 67%, International 33%. By volume: CSD 73.9%, packaged water 20.2%, NCB 5.9%. Low-sugar/no-sugar products ~59% of volumes.
strategy: Leverage PepsiCo brands to penetrate under-served Indian territories and expand rural reach
Strategic acquisitions in Africa/South Asia to consolidate markets and improve operating leverage
Product innovation with low-sugar/zero-sugar variants and new beverage categories
Backward integration and manufacturing optimization for cost efficiency and scale
Strengthen balance sheet through cash generation and debt reduction
annual_report.outlook: Positioned for sustained growth through commissioned greenfield facilities, strong international expansion especially Africa, continued portfolio diversification, and favorable India demographics. CY2025 resilience despite weather confirms business model strength.
annual_report.capex_plans: ₹45bn deployed through CY2025: ₹17bn for four greenfield plants (India), ₹3bn brownfield expansions, ₹13bn international including Twizza (South Africa).
risks: High dependency on PepsiCo franchise agreements; unfavorable renewal terms could adversely impact profitability
Demand cyclicality from macro slowdowns or adverse weather patterns affecting beverage consumption
Health and packaging waste regulations may discriminatorily target soft drinks or increase compliance costs
Raw material supply disruptions or significant price increases could impact business prospects
annual_report.flags: Twizza (South Africa) acquisition pending regulatory approvals by June 2026. CRISIL upgraded long-term credit rating to AAA/Stable.
